anatomy.web: Single Button(variant, size, emphasis, asChild, loading, disabled, ...props) function component wrapping either a native <button> or Slot.Root; ButtonLabel is also exported as a truncatable text slot. Two variants (default/premium) carry `sheen-action`/`foil-value` pseudo-layer classes, the rest are flat cva fills -- the same two-vs-five split.

states.flutter: THE PRESS SCALE DOES NOT SPRING, and Button.dart reproduces the measured hard-cut behaviour deliberately: Transform.scale toggles instantly between 1 and MotionTransforms.buttonPress with 'No controller, no curve, no duration: the flag is the frame' (button.dart lines 1077-1092), matching a driven-pointer trace of the live reference. Colour legs (fill/border/content) DO spring via nested TweenAnimationBuilder/_SpringColors at press's measured 250ms/40ms duration pair on MotionCurves.emphasized.
states.web: `press` in styles/motion.css: `transition: transform var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-emphasized)` (plus background-color/border-color/color/box-shadow/opacity on the same clock) with `&:active, &[data-pressed] { transition-duration: var(--duration-press-in) }` — 250ms out, 40ms in, on cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1).
states.note: RECLASSIFIED after it was measured. The finding was that button.tsx's docstring claims an asymmetric spring while both platforms hard-cut the press. Measured on the button page in the browser: a resting `.press` computes `transition-duration: 0.25s` on `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` — a curve that overshoots and settles — and `.press:active` is present in the built stylesheet setting `transition-duration: var(--duration-press-in)`, which is 40ms. The docstring's '40ms in, 250ms out, springs back' is exactly what the CSS does. Flutter's doc comment is correcting a claim that is true here. ORIGINAL: This is not a Flutter-vs-web divergence in rendered behaviour -- both platforms hard-cut the press scale, and Flutter's implementation is the historically correct one. It is flagged as a gap because the WEB COMPONENT'S OWN DOCSTRING (components/ui/button.tsx lines 12-16, 'springs back over 250ms... overshoots then settles') actively misdescribes its own measured behaviour, and the Flutter file's extensive library-doc correction ('THE PRESS DOES NOT SPRING -- MEASURED') exists specifically to counteract that stale claim. A reader auditing states from the web docstring alone would record the wrong contract; recorded here so the ledger points at the truth (button.dart's own doc, backed by a driven-pointer trace) rather than at button.tsx's uncorrected prose. button.tsx should be corrected or annotated at lines 12-16 to match reality.

disabled.flutter: `_enabled = widget.onPressed != null && !widget.loading` -- loading forces the whole disabled branch (Disabled(disabled: !_enabled, ...), 45% opacity per B11 spec, IgnorePointer instant/not on the colour-spring clock); disabledReason renders a tooltip on hover/tap while disabled, and onDisabledPressed (defaulting to Form.revealFirstError inside a FormScope) fires on a tap while idle-disabled.
disabled.web: `disabled = disabled || loading` (button.tsx L118) drives the native disabled attribute, pulling in disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 from the base cva string, and loading additionally sets data-loading + aria-busy; no built-in disabledReason/tooltip mechanism exists in the web component itself.

interaction.flutter: Keyboard path is wired by hand via Focus.onKeyEvent handling Enter/NumpadEnter/Space (button.dart lines 692-704), explicitly because 'Flutter gives a bare Listener neither' -- reproducing native <button> activation; suppressPressScale/aria-haspopup-equivalent and `expanded`/aria-expanded-equivalent are both ported as explicit boolean props read by the state table.
interaction.web: Native <button> activates on Enter and Space by default; `active:not-aria-[haspopup]:scale-95` and the `aria-expanded:*` classes read real DOM attributes (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded) that DropdownMenuTrigger/PopoverTrigger stamp onto the rendered button via asChild.

semantics.flutter: Semantics(button: true, enabled: _enabled, label: widget.label, excludeSemantics: widget.label != null) -- the library doc states plainly 'aria-busy HAS NO FLUTTER ANALOGUE... There is no flag to set and no role to borrow that would not also announce something the reference does not', so a loading Flutter button announces only enabled:false, never that it is specifically busy/loading.
semantics.web: aria-busy={loading || undefined} is set directly on the native <button> alongside the native disabled attribute, so assistive tech gets both signals: the control is inert AND specifically busy, not merely disabled.
